root.name: Sicilian Defense: Yates Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Bd3

overview: In this Classical Sicilian line White develops the bishop to d3 against ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and ...d6, aiming at castling and f4 or Kh1. Black chooses between ...g6, ...e6 and ...e5 set-ups. I am unsure of the exact Yates move order and its distinctions from the Scheveningen.

white_ideas.idea: Castle kingside and play f4 and Kh1

black_ideas.idea: Play ...g6 or ...e6 as a Dragon or Scheveningen-style set-up

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian with half-open c-file for Black

character.notes: Standard double-edged Sicilian but White's plan is fairly slow.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

character.reason: A standard Open Sicilian line where neither side forces matters early.

structure.reason: Every Sicilian has an asymmetric centre and a half-open c-file.

level.reason: The usual Sicilian plans matter more than a long forced sequence.

plans.reason: Black plays on the half-open c-file.
